post.description:
Create a user and record their consents.

Idempotent on `user_id`: sending the same one twice returns the
existing user rather than failing, because a client retrying a
dropped response should not have to distinguish the two cases.

schema.title: Response Read V1 Users  User Id  Get

patch.description:
Correct a profile.

Age and education feed the norm adjustment, so a correction moves
every *future* cognitive score. Scores already written are untouched —
§9.5 forbids rewriting history, and a percentile that silently changed
under a user would be worse than one that is stale.

schema.title: Response Amend V1 Users  User Id  Patch

delete.description:
Delete the user and everything derived from them (§3.3).

Cascades across events, scores, decisions, summaries, cached features,
journal blobs and their encryption keys, then scans every user-scoped
table and reports what is left. `verified` false means the scan found
residue and needs a human — it is reported, not swallowed.

post.description:
Grant or revoke one purpose.

Both are appended, never updated in place: "was this user consented on
the 4th?" has to stay answerable, and an UPDATE destroys the only
record that could answer it.

What this user still has to do, and what each step unlocks.

Drive the onboarding UI from this rather than from a hardcoded
sequence: when a score gains a component the requirements change here
and the client does not have to be redeployed to match.

Response Submit Trial V1 Assessment Trial Post

post.description:
Close an assessment and score it.

A session that is never closed is not a completed assessment, and the
difference is not cosmetic: `assessment_session_count` drives the
practice-effect correction (§8.3) and the three-session baseline
(§9.4). Without this call a user can finish the whole battery and
still be treated as having done none — their scores never get the
practice term subtracted and their baseline never establishes.

Scoring runs here rather than on a timer so the client can show a
result on the screen the user is already looking at.

post.description:
One check-in: mood, strain, energy, what is affecting you, a note.

The note goes through the safety filter like any free text (§10.1).

The idempotency key is the submission instant, so checking in twice
with the same values records two check-ins rather than rejecting the
second. Idempotency exists to absorb a phone retrying on a dropped
connection — not to stop someone recording that they still feel the
same an hour later.

get.description:
The four headline scores, burnout, and the well-being index.

One call rather than four: the dashboard shows them together, and
splitting it would let the panels disagree by a few seconds of drift.

Liveness. Answers if the process is running and nothing else — a
restart would not fix whatever a readiness failure is reporting, so
the two must not be the same endpoint.

Readiness. Actually reaches the database, because a process that
cannot reach its database serves 500s while reporting itself healthy,
and a reverse proxy has no way to tell.
